plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Space, Year 5 (VC2M5SP02): a grid coordinate system that uses coordinates to locate positions, compared with a grid reference system
plan.shape: compare-two-models: a grid reference (it names a space) beside a coordinate grid (it names a point on the lines), because the switch from spaces to lines is the new idea
plan.criticalFeature: coordinates sit where two lines cross: across first, then up
decisionPoints: the choice check: which grid shows (3, 1)?
the hinge: which point is at (0, 3)?
plan.anchor: across the corridor, then up the stairs: (x, y), and the numbers sit on the lines

studentTools: A ruler and a sharp pencil for every student
Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The anchor on the board: across the corridor, then up the stairs, (x, y)
A large grid drawn or projected for plotting together

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Read and plot points, a coordinates table, a school map, a mistake to fix and a reasoning question.
resources.title: Reading and Plotting Coordinates
resources.subtitle: Across the corridor, then up the stairs.

example.prompt: What are the coordinates of point A?
steps: Start at 0, where the axes meet.

items.prompt: Write the coordinates of each point.
Plot and label these points: P (1, 4), Q (4, 1), R (0, 5), S (7, 3).
items.answer: P, Q, R and S plotted on the lines

items.prompt: Fill the gaps. Across first, then up.

example.prompt: What is at (2, 6) on the school map?
steps: Read the label at that point.

items.prompt: Use the school map to answer.

parts.prompt: What are the coordinates of the oval?
Start at the library. Go 5 across and 4 up. Where are you?

items.prompt: Point T is 6 across and 1 up. Ava wrote its coordinates. Find her mistake and fix it.
work: T is 1 up and 6 across, so T is (1, 6).

items.prompt: Which point sits on the y-axis, the line going up?
items.explain: (0, 5) goes across 0, so it stays on the line going up.

example.prompt: A rectangle has corners at (1, 1), (5, 1) and (5, 3). Where is the fourth corner?
steps: The fourth corner is across from (1, 1) and level with (5, 3).

items.prompt: A square has corners at (2, 2), (6, 2) and (6, 6). Where is the fourth corner?
A rectangle has corners at (0, 1), (3, 1) and (0, 6). Where is the fourth corner?

example.prompt: Points follow the rule: the second number is double the first. What comes after (1, 2), (2, 4)?

items.prompt: Each point follows the rule: the second number is 3 more than the first. Fill the gaps.

steps: Draw a simple shape on a grid, with its corners on the lines.
A partner joins them in order.

items.prompt: Draw a shape with at least 5 corners on squared paper. List its corners in order so a partner can draw it without seeing yours.
items.answer: Check every corner sits where two lines cross and the list is in order, across first.

It does not go up at all. Up 0.

steps: Draw a dot where the lines cross.

slides.notes: Session 1 of our coordinates week: today we read and plot points on a grid.
Before you start, put boards, markers, a ruler and a pencil on every desk. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Measure and name it
prompts: How big is this angle? What is its name?

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with last week's angles.
ASK: How big is this angle, and what is its name?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 140, obtuse
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> finger on the 0 under the arm, count up together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 140 degrees, and that's obtuse,
because it's between 90 and 180. Tick it or fix it.
trap: reading 40 on the wrong scale.
Fix: ask whether it looks obtuse,
and they read again from the 0 on the arm.
notes.prep: Review of Week 1 angles (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

beats: ASK: How big is angle x?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 118
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> trace the straight line, say half turn 180, then subtract. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 118 degrees, because 180 take away 62 is 118.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: subtracting from 360.
Fix: trace the straight line, and they redo it from 180.
notes.prep: Week 1 review: angles on a straight line.

beats: ASK: How big is angle y?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 120
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> add the two angles you know, then count on to 360 together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 120 degrees. 150 and 90 make 240,
and 360 take away 240 is 120. Tick it or fix it.
trap: subtracting from 180.
Fix: trace all the way round, and they redo it from 360.
notes.prep: Week 1 review: angles at a point.

beats: SAY: Now for our four times table.
Write each answer as fast as you can.
ASK: What is 7 times 4?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 28
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> double 7, then double again. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 28. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 24 or 32.
Fix: double 7 to get 14, double again to get 28, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Here's the next one.
ASK: What is 4 times 9?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 36
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> double 9, then double again. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 36. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 32.
Fix: count on one more 4 from 4 times 8, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: Now a division. Think: how many fours make 44?
ASK: What is 44 divided by 4?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 11
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> count up in fours from 40. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 11. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 10.
Fix: check: 10 times 4 is 40,
one more four makes 44, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to read and plot points on a grid using coordinates.
successCriteria: I can find a point on a grid when I am told its coordinates.
I can read and write coordinates, going across first, then up.
I can explain why (2, 5) and (5, 2) are different points.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: This week is all about finding places on a grid.
Today we learn to read and plot points with coordinates.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 finding a point is reachable for everyone; SC2 reading and writing in the right order is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 explaining order is the stretch.

slides.title: Where is the treasure?
slides.prompt: Which square is the treasure in?

beats: POINT to the letters along the bottom, then the numbers up the side.
SAY: Some of you may have used a map like this before.
Each square has a letter and a number.
ASK: Which square is the X in?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: C3
SCAN boards for C3.
80%+ -> say: that names a whole square. Today we name exact points.
Less -> run a finger along to C, then up to 3, together. Re-ask.
SAY: A grid reference names a square, a space.
Today we're going to name points on the lines instead, and that's more exact.
trap: writing 3C.
Fix: say letter first, then number, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: a grid reference names a space, which sets up why coordinates use the lines. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: A pair of numbers that shows exactly where a point is: across first, then up.

notes.answer: a pair of numbers: across first, then up
beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is coordinates. Say it with me: co-or-din-ates.
SAY: Coordinates are a pair of numbers in brackets.
The first number tells us how far across,
and the second tells us how far up.
ASK: Which number do we use first, the across number or the up number?
5 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: across
trap: saying up first.
Fix: act it out: walk across the corridor,
then climb the stairs, and they say it again.
notes.prep: The word the whole week depends on. The anchor goes on the board now: across the corridor, then up the stairs.

slides.title: Read a point
steps: Start at 0, where the two axes meet.

beats: POINT to 0.
SAY: Let me show you how I read where point A is.
I always start at 0, where the two lines meet.
MODEL across, then up.
SAY: First I go across the corridor, along the bottom, to 5.
Then I climb the stairs, up to 3.
ASK: So how would we write the coordinates of A?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (5, 3)
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 5, 3. Across 5, then up 3,
and the numbers sit where the lines cross, not in a square.
trap: writing (3, 5).
Fix: walk it again: across the corridor first,
then up the stairs, and they rewrite it.
notes.stretch: Where would (3, 5) be? Point to it.
notes.help: Put a finger on 0 and slide across before you look up.
notes.prep: The critical feature: across first, then up, on the lines. SC2.

slides.title: Plot a point
steps: Draw a dot where the lines cross.

beats: MODEL plotting (2, 6).
SAY: Now I'll plot a point. My coordinates are 2, 6.
Across to 2 first, then I follow that line up to 6,
and I draw a dot.
POINT to C.
SAY: Now look at C. It uses the same two numbers, the other way round.
ASK: What are the coordinates of C?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (6, 2)
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: C is 6, 2. Swapping the numbers moves the point,
so the order really matters.
trap: putting the dot in the middle of a square.
Fix: trace both lines to where they cross, and they redraw it.
notes.stretch: Find a point where swapping the numbers does not move it.
notes.help: Use a ruler to follow the line up from the across number.
notes.prep: Order matters: (2, 6) and (6, 2) are different places. SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Which grid shows (3, 1)?
slides.prompt: Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: goes up first: reads the numbers in the wrong order
puts the point in a square, like a grid reference

beats: SAY: Here are three grids, each with one point.
Only one of them shows the point 3, 1.
ASK: Which grid shows the point 3, 1?
10 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What went wrong in C?
Less -> act it out on the floor grid, across then up, and re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B. Across 3, then up 1,
and the dot sits where two lines cross.
trap: pointing to C.
Fix: trace the two lines to where they cross, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. A means the order is reversed; C means they still think in squares.

slides.title: What are the coordinates?
slides.ask: What are the coordinates of point P?
slides.pivot: slide a finger across, then up, together on the big grid
slides.followUp: cold call one board: Which number did you write first, and why?

items.say: It's 3, 0. It goes across 3, but it doesn't go up at all.
It's 0, 4. It doesn't go across at all, then up 4.

say: Write the coordinates of P on your board each time.
trap: writing (4, 0) for a point on the line going up.
Fix: ask how far across it goes, and they rewrite it.
notes.stretch: Write the coordinates of the point you would get by swapping the numbers.
notes.help: Draw an arrow across, then an arrow up, before you write.
notes.prep: Guided practice from typical to edge cases: points on each axis. SC2.

notes.answer: B. A means across and up were swapped
beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Read the coordinates carefully: across first.
ASK: Which point is at 0, 3? Write its letter.
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: B
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> start at 0, go across 0, then up 3, together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's B. Across 0, so it stays on the line going up,
then up 3. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing A.
Fix: ask how far across B goes, and they choose again.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone who wrote A starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Read and plot the points on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Which number did you go along first?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: plotting in the squares.
Fix: trace both lines to the crossing, and they redraw it.
notes.stretch: Extension: missing corners, coordinate patterns and a puzzle you design.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: every point is talked through, with a hint on each question.
notes.prep: Independent practice: read, plot, a map and reasoning. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Write the coordinates of K and of L.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: What are the coordinates of K, and of L?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: K (7, 2), L (2, 7)
RECORD who swaps the numbers for K or L.
They start tomorrow's check with the teacher.
trap: writing K (2, 7).
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: two points that use the same numbers, so order is tested.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner how you remember which number comes first.

notes.answer: open - listen for across the corridor, then up the stairs
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can read and write coordinates?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with K and L swapped matters most.
ASK: How do you remember which number comes first?
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: across the corridor, then up the stairs
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow's first check comes from both.
